verdict_reason: The contract change is RIGHT and I re-measured it head-to-head against platonic-rep metrics.py (commit dcd76ba). At every topk the reference accepts (2 <= k <= n) BLME's _cknna is bit-identical to AlignmentMetrics.cknna -- relative error EXACTLY 0.0 at k=n and k=n-1, both estimators, on both a cross pair (N=200, D=64/48, L2-normalised) and a self pair. The estimator-dependent clamp reproduces the paper's only closed-form anchor: with unbiased=False, k=n gives an all-ones mask and CKNNA collapses to biased CKA -- 0.215725018 against an independently computed CKA of 0.215725022, rel 1.95e-08 (and 0.702768769 vs 0.702768820, rel 7.2e-08, on the committed fixture) -- where the old n-1 clamp returned 0.223388895, 3.55% off (4.21% on the fixture). The unbiased half of the branch is a provable no-op rather than a fix: _hsic_unbiased zeroes the diagonal itself, and the k=n-1 mask differs from all-ones ONLY on the diagonal, so k=n and k=n-1 are identical by construction -- confirmed, both equal the official value to rel 0.0 and unbiased CKA to 4.3e-10.
comparable_reason: Not re-swept this round; the prior round's finding stands. All emitted values are ratios in [0,1] and n_points is hard-capped at max_cknna_tokens=2000 with a shared seeded permutation, so token count is matched across layers and models. The residual is depth: min_offdiag_cknna and max_offdiag_cknna are extrema over n(n-1)/2 layer pairs, so deeper models take more draws from the same distribution; the prior round measured a 6-layer model ordering above a 12-layer one, and min_offdiag moving 0.2186 -> 0.1332 (-39%) when num_samples went 25 -> 100 at the SAME n_points=2000. The mean/std summaries are the comparable ones.
github_reason: Re-executed the cloned repo's metrics.py against BLME this round, focusing on the branch that changed. AlignmentMetrics.cknna vs _cknna on N=200 L2-normalised features: rel EXACTLY 0.0 at k=n and k=n-1 for unbiased in {True, False}, on both cross and self pairs. The reference RAISES RuntimeError for k>n (torch.topk cannot select more columns than exist); BLME degrades gracefully to the k=n / k=n-1 limit instead, which is a documented superset of the reference's domain, not a divergence on it. The previously certified results are unchanged: _remove_outliers is bit-identical to metrics.remove_outliers(q=0.95, exact=False), and the full normed->_cknna pipeline matches the official prepare_features->F.normalize->cknna chain to max |difference| 0.0 over gpt2's 12x12 layer matrix.
paper_reason: Huh et al. 2024 App. A state that CKNNA recovers CKA as k -> dim(K). BLME now reproduces it: biased k=n gives 0.215725018 against an independently computed biased CKA of 0.215725022 (rel 1.95e-08) on random data and 0.702768769 vs 0.702768820 (rel 7.2e-08) on the committed fixture. The unbiased k=n limit also lands, at 4.3e-10 against unbiased CKA. The paper publishes no absolute CKNNA value for a language model (Fig. 10 is z-scored), so this limit is the only reproducible published quantity and it is now hit.
confounds_reason: Not re-measured this round. Values are bounded ratios, layer indices are excluded from the emitted keys, and token count is matched at 2000, so there is no direct d_model or vocab channel; the residual is that extremum summaries over n(n-1)/2 layer pairs grow more extreme with depth by construction. The remove_outliers preprocessing damps the massive-activation channel that would otherwise vary by architecture (max |x| per gpt2 layer 100 / 2956 / 330 at layers 0 / 6 / 11, with 5.4-5.9% of entries clamped in every layer).
defects: TEST: the new test_topk_validation CKA anchor is VACUOUS. It asserts _cknna(X, X, topk=n, unbiased=False) == cka_self, but on a SELF pair both sides are identically 1.0 -- the mutual-kNN mask is the same for K and L, so sim_kl == sim_kk == sim_ll for ANY k, and the test's own cka_self reduces to (Kc*Kc).sum()/sqrt((Kc*Kc).sum()^2) = 1.0. Measured on the committed fixture (n=20): the OLD n-1 clamp also returns exactly 1.0, so the assertion passes under the very behaviour it was written to forbid. Use a CROSS pair: _cknna(X, Y, topk=n, unbiased=False) = 0.702768769 against CKA 0.702768820 (rel 7.2e-08) while the n-1 clamp gives 0.673155431 (4.21% off). Only the 'finite, not NaN' half of the test currently has teeth.

The _cknna docstring's return contract is now stale in two places: 'topk: number of nearest neighbours (must be >= 2 and < N)' and 'Returns NaN if the inputs are degenerate (N < topk+1, or HSIC denominator collapses)'. For n > 2 the function no longer returns NaN when n <= topk; it clamps. The inline comment beside the clamp is correct and complete, but the parameter/return docs above it contradict it.

The unbiased arm of the estimator-dependent clamp is a no-op dressed as a fix. _hsic_unbiased fill_diagonal_(0)s both arguments, and the k=n-1 mutual mask is all-ones-except-diagonal, so mask*K and K are indistinguishable to it: k=n and k=n-1 return the same float (verified rel 0.0 against the official at both). The comment 'with unbiased=True the diagonal is -inf, so k = n would select it and k = n-1 IS the largest meaningful neighbourhood' is a correct description of intent but implies a numerical difference that does not exist.

Reachability unchanged: evaluate() returns an error dict when n_points <= topk, so no shipped number goes through this branch. It exists only so the paper's limit is checkable -- which makes the vacuous test the thing that matters here.

The released code masks the RAW Gram and centers inside HSIC; a center-first reading of the paper's Eq. (16)-(17) differs. RE-MEASURED this round on N=200, k=10, biased HSIC: code/BLME form 0.644992 vs center-first form 0.606461, ratio 1.064 -- a 6.4% divergence, NOT the 2.8x I reported last round, which I withdraw. Following the released code is still the right call and the module docstring already names 'metrics.py:cknna' as the definition source; one sentence noting the paper's equation differs would close it.

prepare_features(exact=True), the global sorted quantile used by the packaged platonic/alignment.py API, is still undocumented as the branch NOT taken (BLME matches measure_alignment.py's exact=False default; measured effect on gpt2 max 0.00285 in CKNNA).
sim_kk and sim_ll each depend on one layer only but are recomputed inside every layer PAIR -- 3x redundant O(n^3) work. Still not hoisted.
Non-finite pair values are silently dropped from the summaries with no count emitted, so summaries can rest on different pair counts per model.
